reconcile.note: Gill distinguishes the civil obedience owed to masters from the religious submission and worship reserved for Christ alone.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Should We Serve God Alone?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/serve.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: You were bought with a price. Don't become bondservants of men.
sides.verseText: You were bought with a price. Don't become bondservants of men.

sides.snippet: Servants, obey in all things those who are your masters according to the flesh, not just when they are looking, as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
sides.verseText: Servants, obey in all things those who are your masters according to the flesh, not just when they are looking, as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.
